Board Important – Karnataka 2nd PUC Question Bank

Human Reproduction is one of the highest-yield chapters in 2nd PUC Biology, NEET and KCET – all six topics (Male RS, Female RS, Gametogenesis, Menstrual Cycle, Fertilisation, Pregnancy & Parturition) are tested almost equally, so no topic can be skipped.
~15–18 marksOne of the highest-weightage chapters in the Reproduction unit, across theory and diagram questions
6 × 5 MTestis structure & sperm pathway, mammary gland structure, oogenesis, four phases of menstrual cycle, zygote→implantation & sex determination, parturition mechanism
6 × 3 MAccessory glands & seminal plasma, oviduct structure, hormonal control of spermatogenesis, role of corpus luteum, process of fertilisation, placenta formation & functions
6 × 2 MScrotum & thermoregulation, uterine wall layers, spermiogenesis vs spermiation, menarche & menopause, implantation & its significance, colostrum & breastfeeding

⭐⭐⭐ Top priority – almost always asked (5 marks)

  • Structure of testis & path of sperm to the exterior (5 M) – testes lie in the scrotum, 2–2.5°C cooler than body temperature (needed for spermatogenesis); each testis has ~250 lobules, each with 1–3 seminiferous tubules lined by spermatogonia and Sertoli cells; interstitial Leydig cells secrete androgens. Trace the path: seminiferous tubules → rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens → ejaculatory duct → urethra → urethral meatus.
  • Structure & hormonal control of the mammary gland (5 M) – each breast has 15–20 lobes made of alveoli (modified sweat glands); flow of milk is alveoli → mammary tubules → mammary duct → mammary ampulla → lactiferous duct → nipple. Prolactin (anterior pituitary) controls secretion; oxytocin (posterior pituitary) controls ejection/let-down.
  • Oogenesis with follicular development (5 M) – oogonia form only in foetal life → arrested at prophase-I as primary oocytes → primary follicle → secondary follicle (theca layer added) → tertiary follicle (fluid-filled antrum, meiosis-I completes unequally into secondary oocyte + first polar body) → Graafian follicle (zona pellucida forms) → ovulation.
  • Four phases of the menstrual cycle with hormones (5 M) – menstrual phase (days 1–5, endometrial breakdown if no fertilisation) → follicular/proliferative phase (rising LH & FSH; oestrogen regenerates endometrium) → ovulatory phase (LH surge ruptures Graafian follicle around day 14) → luteal/secretory phase (corpus luteum secretes progesterone, maintains endometrium).
  • Zygote to implantation & sex determination (5 M) – zygote → cleavage (2, 4, 8, 16 blastomeres) → morula → blastocyst (outer trophoblast + inner cell mass) → implantation in the endometrium → pregnancy. Female is XX (all ova carry X); male is XY (50% X, 50% Y sperm) – so the father's sperm decides the child's sex.
  • Neuroendocrine mechanism of parturition (5 M) – signals from the fully developed foetus and placenta cause mild contractions (foetal ejection reflex) → oxytocin released from the maternal posterior pituitary → stronger myometrial contractions → still more oxytocin (positive feedback) → expulsion of the baby, then the placenta.

⭐⭐ High priority – frequently asked (3 marks)

  • Accessory glands & composition of seminal plasma (3 M) – seminal vesicles + prostate + bulbourethral glands secrete seminal plasma (fructose, calcium, enzymes), about 60% of semen volume; fructose gives energy, alkaline pH (~7.4) neutralises vaginal acidity, bulbourethral secretion lubricates the penis.
  • Structure & functions of the oviduct (3 M) – infundibulum (fimbriae collect the ovum after ovulation) → ampulla (usual site of fertilisation, at the ampullary–isthmic junction) → isthmus (narrow, joins the uterus).
  • Hormonal regulation of spermatogenesis (3 M) – hypothalamic GnRH → anterior pituitary releases LH & FSH; LH (ICSH in males) acts on Leydig cells → testosterone → stimulates spermatogenesis; FSH acts on Sertoli cells → factors that help spermiogenesis.
  • Role of the corpus luteum (3 M) – forms from the ruptured Graafian follicle in the luteal phase; secretes progesterone, which maintains the endometrium; if fertilisation fails it degenerates → progesterone falls → menstruation; if fertilisation occurs, it is retained.
  • Process of fertilisation (3 M) – sperm and ovum meet at the ampullary–isthmic junction; the sperm induces changes in the zona pellucida that block polyspermy; acrosomal enzymes let it penetrate; the secondary oocyte completes meiosis-II; haploid sperm and ovum nuclei fuse (syngamy) to form the diploid zygote.
  • Formation & functions of the placenta (3 M) – chorionic villi from the trophoblast interdigitate with uterine tissue to form the placenta, connected to the embryo by the umbilical cord; supplies O2/nutrients, removes CO2/waste, and acts as an endocrine organ secreting hCG, hPL, oestrogens and progestogens (relaxin later).

⭐ Two-mark favourites – learn as clean pairs

  • Why the testes lie in the scrotum – kept 2–2.5°C cooler than body temperature, essential for spermatogenesis.
  • Three layers of the uterine wall – perimetrium (outer), myometrium (thick muscle, contracts during labour), endometrium (inner, cyclic changes, site of implantation).
  • Spermiogenesis (spermatid → motile sperm) vs spermiation (release of sperm from Sertoli cells into the tubule lumen).
  • Menarche (first menstruation at puberty, 12–15 yrs) vs menopause (permanent cessation, ~50 yrs).
  • Implantation – trophoblast attaches to and embeds in the endometrium, leading to pregnancy.
  • Colostrum – first few days' milk, rich in IgA antibodies; gives the newborn its initial immunity, hence breast-feeding is recommended.
Answer-writing tip: for every "describe the structure" 5-mark question in this chapter, answer in the order Location → Parts named in sequence → Function of each part, and always finish a duct/pathway question with the full arrow-chain (e.g. rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens → ejaculatory duct → urethra) – examiners award marks per correctly ordered structure, not just for naming them.
Never lose these marks: don't mix up look-alike pairs – LH surge (triggers ovulation) vs FSH (drives follicle growth & spermiogenesis); prolactin (controls milk secretion) vs oxytocin (controls milk ejection AND uterine contractions in parturition); primary oocyte vs secondary oocyte; and spermiogenesis vs spermiation. Write these exactly as paired definitions and you rarely drop marks.

Reproductive System Anatomy

Fig 2.1 — Male Reproductive System (L.S.) 5 M ★★★ Top Priority
Label: testis (in scrotum), epididymis, vas deferens, seminal vesicle, prostate, bulbourethral gland, urethra, penis. Show the duct pathway clearly: seminiferous tubules → rete testis → vasa efferentia → epididymis → vas deferens → ejaculatory duct → urethra.
View page 27 in NCERT PDF →
Fig 2.2 — Female Reproductive System (L.S.) 5 M ★★★ Top Priority
Label: ovary, fallopian tube with infundibulum/fimbriae/ampulla/isthmus, uterus (fundus, body, cervix), vagina. Mark the ampullary–isthmic junction as the usual site of fertilisation.
View page 29 in NCERT PDF →

Gametogenesis Flowcharts

Fig 2.3 — Spermatogenesis Flowchart 3 – 5 M ★★☆ High Priority
Draw as a branching flowchart: spermatogonium (2n) → primary spermatocyte (2n) → [meiosis I] → 2 secondary spermatocytes (n) → [meiosis II] → 4 spermatids (n) → spermiogenesis → 4 spermatozoa. Label spermiation as the release of sperm from Sertoli cells.
View page 32 in NCERT PDF →
Fig 2.4 — Oogenesis Flowchart 5 M ★★★ Top Priority
Oogonium (2n, foetal life only) → primary oocyte (arrested at prophase-I) → primary follicle → secondary follicle (theca added) → tertiary follicle (antrum forms, meiosis-I completes unequally) → secondary oocyte + first polar body → Graafian follicle (zona pellucida) → ovulation. Label meiosis-II as completing only after fertilisation.
View page 32 in NCERT PDF →

Cycles & Cellular Structures

Fig 2.5 — Menstrual Cycle & Hormone Level Graph 5 M ★★★ Top Priority
Plot LH, FSH, oestrogen and progesterone levels across the 28-day cycle on the X-axis, marking the four phases: menstrual (1–5), follicular/proliferative (5–13), ovulatory (~14, LH surge), luteal/secretory (15–28). Show the LH surge peak precisely at ovulation.
View page 33 in NCERT PDF →
Fig 2.6 — Structure of a Sperm 2 – 3 M ★★☆ High Priority
Label head (nucleus + acrosome with hydrolytic enzymes), neck (proximal/distal centrioles), middle piece (mitochondria spirally arranged, provides energy for motility), tail (flagellum), and the plasma membrane covering the whole body.
View page 32 in NCERT PDF →
